new_symbol_range_suggestions.metabolic_heat_production: positive heat-production state remaining near baseline during mild recovery, plausibly between a modestly suppressed level and the initial baseline value
new_symbol_range_suggestions.metabolic_suppression_strength: dimensionless, typically between 0 and 1 so the heat-elevated equilibrium metabolic production remains nonnegative
new_symbol_range_suggestions.metabolic_adjustment_time: positive and typically comparable to or longer than slow_recruitment_time during mild recovery

derivation_notes: The constant-metabolism assumption is relaxed by promoting metabolic_heat_production to a state that relaxes toward a lower temperature-dependent equilibrium only when core temperature is above the set point. Its initial condition is kept at the parent baseline value so the trajectory starts on the parent's unsuppressed branch and any phase effect must develop dynamically rather than being imposed at t=0.
change_summary: Metabolic heat production is no longer fixed; it slowly decreases during sustained mild heat elevation and recovers toward baseline near or below the set point. This creates phase-dependent cooling at matched thermal states because the inward heat-production term now carries trajectory history.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: metabolic_heat_production is constant across the entire trajectory and does not adapt to sustained elevation of core temperature.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Slow heat-induced suppression of thermogenic/metabolic heat production during recovery, operating in parallel with delayed heat-loss recruitment under otherwise fixed ambient conditions.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when metabolic_suppression_strength = 0, or in the fixed-state limit where metabolic_heat_production remains at its initial baseline value throughout the trajectory.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping dT_c_dt(T_c,H,H_slow) uses a fixed metabolic_heat_production, so all temperature recovery is governed only by heat-loss recruitment and the net cooling drive at a given thermal state is independent of recovery phase.
response_change.child_relation: Allow metabolic heat production to undergo slow first-order suppression after mild heat elevation, so dT_c_dt at the same T_c, H, and H_slow can differ between early and late recovery because internal heat generation is lower later in the trajectory.
response_change.observable_effect: For mild above-set-point recoveries under fixed environment, late recovery can cool faster than the parent predicts even after heat-loss factors have begun relaxing, because transient metabolic suppression reduces inward heat flux.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable for mild but sustained above-set-point excursions where T_c - thermal_set_point is positive for long enough that a slower autonomic suppression of metabolic heat production can develop; weak or negligible for near-baseline trajectories and very short perturbations.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as modest extra late-phase cooling during recoveries with longer residence above the set point; in holdout, the same effect extends to trajectories with similar amplitudes but different durations, producing duration-dependent phase separation at matched T_c.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the metabolic-suppression amplitude to zero or its adjustment time to zero/infinity such that metabolic_heat_production remains effectively constant.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A fixed parameter cannot encode trajectory-history-dependent internal heat generation. To create an observable phase-dependent change in dT_c_dt under the same environmental conditions, metabolic_heat_production must be allowed to evolve as a state.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Slow heat-induced suppression of thermogenic/metabolic heat production during recovery, operating in parallel with delayed heat-loss recruitment under otherwise fixed ambient conditions.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the coefficient of the existing heat-balance production term becomes a history-dependent state, creating phase-separated target values at matched thermal states that cannot be obtained from a single static metabolic parameter.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: metabolic_heat_production is constant across the entire trajectory and does not adapt to sustained elevation of core temperature.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: metabolic_heat_production is an internal state that slowly relaxes toward a lower above-set-point equilibrium during mild heat recovery.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when metabolic_suppression_strength = 0, or in the fixed-state limit where metabolic_heat_production remains at its initial baseline value throughout the trajectory.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compare trajectories that attain similar T_c and similar effective_heat_loss_factor = (1 - slow_effector_weight)*H + slow_effector_weight*H_slow but differ in prior residence time above thermal_set_point. The child predicts more negative dT_c_dt later in the longer-hotter-phase trajectory because metabolic_heat_production has been suppressed, whereas the parent predicts the same dT_c_dt at matched T_c, H, and H_slow.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting one shared constant metabolic_heat_production in the parent cannot produce duration-dependent phase separation at matched T_c, H, and H_slow, because the parent target mapping is algebraically memoryless once those states are fixed. Parameter retuning can shift all phases together but cannot make late recovery cooler faster than early recovery under the same observed thermal state without an evolving metabolic state.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable for mild but sustained above-set-point excursions where T_c - thermal_set_point is positive for long enough that a slower autonomic suppression of metabolic heat production can develop; weak or negligible for near-baseline trajectories and very short perturbations.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as modest extra late-phase cooling during recoveries with longer residence above the set point; in holdout, the same effect extends to trajectories with similar amplitudes but different durations, producing duration-dependent phase separation at matched T_c.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the metabolic-suppression amplitude to zero or its adjustment time to zero/infinity such that metabolic_heat_production remains effectively constant.
evolution_plan.promotion_reason: A fixed parameter cannot encode trajectory-history-dependent internal heat generation. To create an observable phase-dependent change in dT_c_dt under the same environmental conditions, metabolic_heat_production must be allowed to evolve as a state.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model assumes constant metabolic heat production during recovery, omitting the plausible slow reduction in endogenous heat production that accompanies passive recovery from mild heat load.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: metabolic_heat_production is constant across the entire trajectory and does not adapt to sustained elevation of core temperature.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Slow heat-induced suppression of thermogenic/metabolic heat production during recovery, operating in parallel with delayed heat-loss recruitment under otherwise fixed ambient conditions.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent already includes fast and slow heat-loss effectors, so its scored target mapping is effectively single-phase: once T_c, H, and H_slow are specified, dT_c_dt is fully determined by a constant inward metabolic term minus heat loss. A realistic next refinement is to relax the constant-metabolism assumption, not to add another decorative heat-loss branch. Under fixed humidity, clothing, activity, and ambient temperature, mild heat exposure can still transiently suppress internal heat generation during recovery. This changes the target mapping itself, not only an auxiliary trajectory, because dT_c_dt directly depends on metabolic_heat_production. The concrete distinguishing condition is to compare recoveries that reach similar T_c and similar effective heat-loss factor but differ in how long they have remained above the set point. The parent with one shared parameter set predicts the same dT_c_dt at matched T_c, H, and H_slow regardless of phase; the child predicts more negative dT_c_dt later in a prolonged recovery due to reduced metabolic input. This is admissible for mild positive thermal_error on the scale already activating H_slow, and it remains limited: if excursions are too small or brief, the added process may be practically unobservable.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make the coefficient of an existing process depend on a declared quantity.

states.rhs: (exp((heat_loss_sensitivity + heat_loss_curvature*(T_c - thermal_set_point)**2)*(T_c - thermal_set_point)) - H)/((thermoeffector_adjustment_time)/(1 + recruitment_time_acceleration*Piecewise((0, T_c - thermal_set_point <= 0), ((T_c - thermal_set_point)/(recruitment_activation_scale + (T_c - thermal_set_point)), True))))
states.description: Fast aggregate thermoeffector heat-loss factor with delayed recruitment toward its temperature-dependent equilibrium and faster saturating recruitment when core temperature is above the set point

states.rhs: (1 + (exp((heat_loss_sensitivity + heat_loss_curvature*(T_c - thermal_set_point)**2)*(T_c - thermal_set_point)) - 1)*Piecewise((0, T_c - thermal_set_point <= 0), ((T_c - thermal_set_point)/(slow_recruitment_threshold + (T_c - thermal_set_point)), True)) - H_slow)/slow_recruitment_time

Whole-body metabolic heat production state that slowly decreases during sustained above-set-point heating and returns toward baseline otherwise

scenario_text: Track core body temperature during recovery from a mild thermal displacement under constant environmental conditions. The body stores heat while fixed metabolic production and temperature-dependent heat loss determine the net rate of temperature change. In the baseline model, aggregate thermoregulatory heat loss changes smoothly around a fixed thermal set point, producing monotonic relaxation. Humidity, clothing, activity, and ambient temperature remain fixed throughout each trajectory.
